title: GSB literal: owner rulings for the scripted layer (supplied articles/copulas, he/it heuristic, ὅς = which, shared glosses)
description: Pilot ursinia-vff.22 (gsb/literal/README.md). Decisions the generator makes that need the owner: (1) it supplies no English articles or copulas by itself ("In beginning", "darkness over the abyss"); hand drafts supply [the]/[a]/[was]; overrides add them one by one (31 of 66 Gen 1-3 overrides). Rule? (2) third-singular pronouns he/she/it are chosen by nearest earlier agreeing noun (person nouns flagged (person) in glosses); verb-ending pronouns unbracketed as in the hand drafts; repeated after every καί ("and he sanctified it"). (3) ὅς always "which", also for persons (hand drafts: "whom"). (4) present indicative simple present ("goes out"), hand draft progressive. (5) glosses that now share an English word: ἀγαθός/καλός good, οἶκος/οἰκία house, οὔτε/οὐδέ nor, ἥκω come; φέρω carry (ἄγω has bring). (6) ἡμέρα μία "one day" (generator moves adjectives) vs hand "day one".
close_reason: Owner ruled (rule 16a); implemented: no default supplied articles/copulas, he/she/it for unstated subjects (none after καί, gender only from the clause, impersonal list in data), his/its for masc/neut-ambiguous forms, who/whom via (person) antecedent. Overrides pruned.

Output: gsb/sources/swete/NN-<book-id>.tsv (chapter, verse, text as printed). Method to be settled by a pilot on Genesis 1-3 and OG Daniel 1: independent readings from the page images (archive.org OCR layer, fresh OCR, model reading of the image), collated, disagreements settled against the image and logged. Third-party transcriptions never enter the repo.

title: GSB literal generator: rule faults from Genesis 29-50
description:
Rule faults reported by the 11 translators of Genesis 29-50 (2026-11-28). De-duplicated, most damaging first, one example each. All false instances in Genesis 29-50 are worked around by overrides or pins; these are what the generator (scripts/lib/gsb-literal.scm) should do instead. Pins whose `why` names a rule fault can be dropped once it is fixed.

1. Neuter plural subject: read as the object, or its singular verb gets "he/she/it". 30:38-42 (sheep became objects of "craved"); 43:30 "his bowels was being twisted together"; 40:17 "the birds ... he/she/it was devouring"; 31:8, 32:21, 49:24, 50:9.
2. Indeclinable name after a noun is always made genitive; apposition case/helper wrong. 35:9 "God of Jacob appeared" (Jacob dative); 29:29 / 46:25 "gave Rachel to his daughter"; 36 passim "chief of Teman" (~33 overrides); 47:22 "gave present to the priests of Pharaoh" (Pharaoh the giver); apposition after a preposition gets "of": 29:18 "concerning Rachel of your daughter of the younger", 49:29 "Ephron of Hittite", 45:21 "by Pharaoh of the king".
3. Accusative subject of a transitive articular infinitive read as its object. 38:17 "until sending you" (= until your sending); 38:28 "in bearing her"; 44:31 "in seeing him"; 29:19; 48:7 τοῦ ἐλθεῖν Ἐφράθα "of Ephrath's coming" (destination made subject).
4. Subject move strands pieces: apposition name left behind 32:4 "So your servant says Jacob", 45:9, 43:27 "If your father is healthy the older"; possessive stranded 49:24, 50:7; καί-joined adjective 41:7; predicate absorbed 47:19 "we and our earth servants will be"; crosses into a relative clause 38:25; split after adverb+genitive 45:10; first of two καί stranded 43:8.
5. Negation stranded when postpositive δέ moves before the subject (reverses sense): 40:23 "Not but the chief cupbearer remembered Joseph"; 31:32.
6. ἄν with a past (aorist/imperfect) indicative rendered "ever" instead of unreal "would have": 31:27 "I sent out ever you"; 30:27, 31:42, 43:10, 44:8.
7. Predicates around γίνομαι/εἰμί: predicate adjective before γίνομαι not moved after it (rule 2a for εἰμί only): 38:11 "until great Shelah come to be my son"; predicate genitive moved with subject 47:20 "the earth of Pharaoh came to be"; anarthrous Κύριος after εἰμί taken as predicate 39:2 "And was [the] Lord with Joseph"; existential εἰμί/γίνομαι with anarthrous plural subject gets "they": 29:16 "they were two daughters", 46:12 "they came to be sons of Perez"; impersonal "it" given to a plural 41:21.
8. Speech boundaries: capital common noun as place name taken as speech 33:17 "departs into, Tents"; 32:31 εἶδος; name opening speech not seen 34:8, 30:13 "Happy Leah I"; question mark of quoted speech applied to the frame 42:22 "I did not speak ... Shall you wrong the lad?".
9. Genitive absolute variants: pronoun first 29:6 "Further of him/it of speaking"; subject before participle 44:14, 44:26, 44:34; after a moved subject 50:17 "And Joseph they speaking wept"; followed by an object 44:4 "But having gone forth they the city".
10. Questions: τί + τοῦτο with third person verb 42:28 "What did this God make to us?"; with a relative clause 37:10; τί + demonstrative + ἐστιν 33:5 "What these to you is?"; no inversion with a pronoun between τί and verb 30:31, 38:16 "What to me you will give"; οὐ-questions not inverted 37:13.
11. Subjunctives: deliberative after τί gives "let us" 44:16; outside a μή question 34:31 "they use"; negated subjunctive of εἰμί after ὃ ἐάν reads as command 30:33 "every which ever do not be speckled"; subjunctive coordinated with a future 43:4 "we will go down and let us buy".
12. Relative after a non-agreeing nearest noun is "which" for persons: 35:3 "God ..., which was with me"; 35:26, 36:5, 46:15, 46:20, 46:22.
13. Double negation: οὐ + verb + οὐδείς gives "not ... no one" 41:44, 45:1; nominative οὐδείς before its verb not the subject 39:11.
14. Possessive gerund fails with something between subject and infinitive: 35:17 "in the severely her to bear"; 39:9 "because of the you his/its woman to be"; 42:16; 34:15 "in being circumcised of you every male".
15. Article agreement: indeclinable numeral after its article raises article-disagrees (αἱ ἑπτὰ βόες, ~10 tag overrides in 41; 31:33); adverb between article and noun 35:4 "the today days", 29:34 "In the now to season".
16. κύριος: articular κύριος always "Lord" for a human master (dozens of overrides 39-45); "[the]" still supplied with an (english "lord") override 45:8 "[the] lord of all his house", 49:23.
17. Case helpers: dative helper put on moved adjective 39:14 "to great voice"; verb's (genitive) field ignored when an object intervenes 39:12 "pulled him of his garments", or on ADV 36 ἐπέκεινα; genitive of comparison 48:19 "greater of it"; genitive participle agreeing with an object gets "of" 31:1, 37:17 "I heard them of saying"; ἐν γῇ Αἰγύπτῳ "in earth to Egypt" 46:20, 46:34; genitive plural of a name-sense noun singular 46:34 "of Egyptian"; plural possessive 29:8 "shepherds's"; genitive of age with numeral 50:26.
18. Word order: article+αὐτοῦ+noun 41:11 "the its dream", τῶν αὐτοῦ 41:43; ὁ θεὸς ὁ ἐμός 49:25 "my [one] God"; ἐπὶ τοῖς ἐκείνων κλήροις 48:6; demonstrative after article+adj+noun 39:9 "the evil utterance this", 37:24; article+adjective after a possessive 44:2 "my goblet the silver"; compound numeral after noun 47:28 "years ten seven"; object pronoun before verb 48:4 "I you will grow", 32:9; τοιαύτη τις split 39:11; adverb ἔτι + subject 29:7.
19. (voice active) on a lemma also flips a true passive: 48:16 ἐπικληθήσεται "my name will call upon".
20. Small: ἐπιπίπτω "fall upon upon" 50:1; particle verb with noun object 49:15 "put under his/its shoulder"; two δέ "but but" 48:6; capital after a pinned verse that ends in ; or , 41:21, 47:21; Μή μοι γένοιτο 44:17 "Not to me it may come to be"; κἀγώ after a verb "And I" 30; two overrides on one word silently replace each other (should be a check error) 32:18.
21. Spelling lists (%stress-initial / %double): interpret, hunger, plunder, slaughter, overpower, loosen.
notes: From the independent read (step 3), more faults worked around by pins: apposition after a comma left behind when the subject moves (34:2); articular participle subject of existential εἰμί moved before the verb (41:8, 41:24); accusative subject of an infinitive in reported speech read as object (41:15); object pronoun between pronoun subject and verb stays before the verb (48:4 'I you will grow'); genitive pronoun before preposition + articular noun not taken as possessor (50:21 'spoke of them into the heart'); indeclinable name before its noun not read as genitive (50:23 'saw Ephraim little children'). Also: articular κύριος for a human master is always 'Lord' (~20 more (english "lord") overrides in 43-47).

title: Markdown extension: shorthand syntax that auto-links to an anchored target
description:
Writing a long document with a reference inventory means hand-writing the same
`[_Politics_](http://classics.mit.edu/Aristotle/politics.html)` link at every
mention. Want a shorthand that resolves to a declared target instead.

## Shape

Some special syntax at the call site, e.g. `{{politics}}` or `[[politics]]`, that
resolves to a target declared once — either an anchor elsewhere in the same
document, or a URL declared in a frontmatter/definition block. Exact syntax is
open; it must not collide with `[label](href)`, `[^footnote]`, or the existing
`{#id}` anchor marker.

## Prerequisite: `{#id}` anchors on list items

`split-trailing-anchor` (md.scm:267) already parses a trailing `{#id}` marker, but
it is only wired into headings (md.scm:89) and paragraphs (md.scm:288). List items
do not support it.

This matters because reference inventories are lists. In
`templates/bible/theology/monarchy/outline/index.md` the Part IX inventory is an
ordered list of ~150 works, and the only linkable targets are the seven `###`
subsection headings. Body citations therefore link to a whole subsection instead of
to the entry for the work being cited. Per-item anchors are what makes the
shorthand actually precise.

## Also worth deciding

Whether the shorthand's link text comes from the target (so the label is written
once) or is supplied at the call site, e.g. `[[politics|_Politics_ III.12]]`.
Citations frequently need a locator that the target does not carry.

## Motivation

The monarchy outline currently has ~86 hand-written citation links in its body.
Every one of them was applied mechanically and every one has to be maintained by
hand when a URL changes.

## Related

Follows the same "make prose into links without markdown syntax" goal as the
confession auto-linking bead, but it is generic rather than domain-specific.
notes: Implemented as CommonMark reference links rather than a bespoke [[key]] syntax: [label][key], [label][] and shortcut [label], with [key]: url "title" definitions. Standard markdown already solves 'declare a destination once, cite it many times', so no new syntax was invented and other tooling understands the result. An unresolved key keeps its literal text, which is what leaves the outline's [CLAIM]/[EV]/[GAP] markers untouched. Prerequisite shipped too: {#id} anchors now work on list items (split-trailing-anchor was already there, only wired to headings and paragraphs), so a reference definition can point at a single inventory entry.
close_reason: Closed

title: Support footnotes in the markdown renderer
description:
The markdown renderer has no footnote support, so both halves of the syntax render
as literal text.

## Current behavior

`templates/bible/theology/monarchy/draft/index.md` uses seven footnotes. Rendering
it emits the raw markers verbatim — `[^1]` through `[^7]` each appear twice in the
output HTML (once at the call site, once in the Notes section) with no links and no
`<a>` tags at all.

## Scope

- Inline reference `[^label]` becomes a superscript link to the definition.
- Definition line `[^label]: text` is collected out of the body flow.
- Definitions render as an ordered list at the end of the document, each with a
  back-link to its call site.
- Definition bodies go through `parse-inline` (they contain emphasis and links —
  see the draft's Notes section).
- Labels are arbitrary strings, not just integers; number the rendered output by
  order of first reference rather than by label.
- Unreferenced definitions and undefined references should degrade to plain text
  rather than erroring.

## Implementation notes

- `parse-inline` (md.scm:143) is where the `[^label]` call site is recognized; it
  must be attempted before `parse-inline-link-at`, since both start with `[`.
- Collection is a document-level concern, so the definition pass belongs in
  `parse-markdown` / `md->html` rather than inline parsing.
- Generated ids must not collide with `text->id` heading anchors; prefix them
  (`fn-1`, `fnref-1`).
- Add a fixture pair under `scripts/lib/sxml/test/md/` and regenerate with
  `make test/regenerate`.
close_reason: Closed

title: Support tables in the markdown renderer
description:
`parse-markdown` (`scripts/lib/md.scm:293`) handles headings, ordered/unordered
lists, fenced code, blockquotes and paragraphs. There is no table support, so
GitHub-flavored pipe tables render as literal text with visible `|` characters.

## Scope

Parse GFM pipe tables into `(table (thead ...) (tbody ...))` SXML:

```
| Author | Work | Date |
| ------ | ---- | ---- |
| Aristotle | _Politics_ | c. 350 BCE |
```

- Header row, delimiter row, body rows.
- Honor the delimiter row's alignment colons (`:--`, `:-:`, `--:`) as `style="text-align:..."`
  or an alignment class.
- Cell contents go through `parse-inline`, so emphasis and links work inside cells.
- Ragged rows: pad or truncate to the header's column count rather than erroring.

## Notes

- `markdownlint` config already sets MD013 `line_length: 120`; wide tables will
  trip it, so check whether MD013's `tables: false` option should be set in
  `.markdownlint.yaml`.
- The theme stylesheet (`/shared/styles/openword-theme.css`) has no table styling
  yet — needs at least borders and cell padding, and horizontal scroll on narrow
  viewports.
- Add a fixture pair under `scripts/lib/sxml/test/md/` and regenerate with
  `make test/regenerate`.

## Motivation

The monarchy research references are CSVs served as raw asset downloads
(`assets/bible/theology/monarchy/research/references/*.csv`). With table support
they could render as readable on-page tables instead.

title: Auto-link confession notations the way scripture references are linked
description:
`scripts/lib/md.scm` already turns bare scripture references in prose into links:
`linkify-scripture` (md.scm:533-577) walks the parsed SXML, matches book names via
`match-book-at`, and emits anchors against `%scripture-base-url` using
`chapter-anchor` / `verse-anchor`. Pages opt out with `scripture-links: false` in
frontmatter.

Do the same for confessional citations, so writing `1689 ch. 23` or `WCF 22.3` in
prose produces a link with no markdown syntax.

## Forms to recognize

- Second London Baptist Confession: `1689 ch. 23`, `LBCF 23`, `LBCF 23.4`, `2LBCF 24.1`
- Westminster Confession: `WCF 22`, `WCF 23.3`, `Westminster Confession ch. 22`
- Catechisms: Baptist Catechism (1695) and Heidelberg by question number (`HC Q.101`)

Chapter-only and chapter.paragraph should both work, matching how the scripture
linker handles chapter vs. verse.

## Prerequisite

There is nothing in the repo to link *to* — the reference CSVs under
`assets/bible/theology/monarchy/research/references/` contain no confessional
documents. This needs a decision first:

1. Host the confession texts as site content (mirrors the Bible versions approach,
   gives stable in-site anchors, most work), or
2. Link out to canonical public texts (fast, but no anchors per paragraph).

Option 1 is what makes the scripture linker work well and is probably the right
target.

## Reuse notes

`linkify-scripture-node` deliberately skips URLs, existing links, code spans, raw
passthrough, and headings (md.scm:558-573) — a confession linker must respect the
same exclusions, so factor that traversal rather than duplicating it.

## Motivation

`templates/bible/theology/monarchy/outline/index.md` cites the 1689 and Westminster
about 25 times in prose. Those are currently hand-linked to a section anchor, which
is a workaround, not a destination.
notes: Links out to baptistconfession.org, which hosts one paragraph per page. NOTE: the wcf1646 prefix in the original request 404s; the live path is /wcf/{ch}.{par}. Confirmed by chapter count -- /33.1 is 404 (1689 has 32 chapters) while /wcf/33.1 is 200 (WCF has 33). title: GSB: checker rule for keep-the-ambiguity (names/pronouns not in the Greek)
description: Flag a literal segment aligned to οὗτος/ἐκεῖνος whose text has a personal pronoun or name and no 'this/that/these/those'; flag a proper name (gloss of a sense named 'name', or God/Lord) in a literal or aligned-readable segment whose refs lack that lemma; for plain-string readable, flag when a name occurs more often than in the literal layer. Found feasible during the Genesis 1-3 pilot (ursinia-vff.4).
notes: Done (agent, 2026-11-26). Rules in check-chapter (scripts/lib/gsb-translation.scm), tested: (1) demonstrative (οὗτος/ἐκεῖνος/ὅδε) aligned to English with a personal pronoun or name and no this/that/these/those -> error (literal and aligned readable; literal counts the word's (cont N) parts); (2) a name (capitalized gloss of a sense named name, or God/Lord) in a segment whose Greek lacks that lemma -> error, supplied segments included; (3) plain readable: a name more often than in the literal -> error; literal demonstrative rendered this/that/these/those but readable has none of those words -> warning only. Drafts: 0 errors; 1 warning, Gen 3:17 (readable drops 'of this' τούτου: 'from which alone'). Known blind spot: the warning is fooled by an unrelated 'that' (Gen 3:11 readable also drops τούτου μόνου but says 'that you are naked'). Genesis readables are plain strings, so rules 1-2 on the readable layer only bite in John 1.

description: scripts/gsb-site.scm maps ps->psalm and jer->jeremiah, so #psalm-23-1 on the GSB page is LXX Ps 23 (= Heb 24). Decide with the versification decision (ursinia-vff.8): keep, use own slugs, or add common-numbering aliases.
notes:
Psalms transcribed 2026-11-28 (leaves v2 233-435). WHAT THE TABLE CONTAINS: gsb/sources/swete/25-ps.tsv keeps Swete's own Septuagint numbering only: chapters 1-151 = LXX psalm numbers, verses = Swete's printed numbers; NO versification.tsv rows for ps and no {=c:v} markers in any Psalms page file. Verse 1 of a titled psalm is the superscription (page marker {T}); where the margin prints 1 beside the first full-size line (Ps 14, 22-27, 31, 34, 36, 42, 49, 65, 70-73, 77-78, 81, 85-86, 89-90, 92-100, 102-106, 108-113, 118-138, 142-145, 149, 151 ...) the title and that line share verse 1. Swete prints no number for: 43:8, 54:6, 63:3, 115:5, 117:4, 118:51, 135:23 (B lacks them; {n!} in the page files), so those verses are absent. WHERE SWETE PRINTS THE HEBREW NUMBERS: from Ps 10 on, beside each Roman numeral in the outer margin, '(N)' = Hebrew psalm (XIV (XV) ... CXLVI (CXLVII); none from 147 on, where LXX 147-150 match or the Hebrew is given by verse); Hebrew verse numbers in parentheses in the margin where the division differs (Ps 9:22-39 = '(X) (1)'-'(18)' i.e. Heb 10:1-18; Ps 113:9-26 = Heb 115:1-18; Ps 115:1-10 = Heb 116:10-19; Ps 147:1-9 = Heb 147:12-20) and ~38 in-text '(n)' marks where a Hebrew verse starts inside Swete's verse (e.g. 7:11, 9:25, 17:?, 113:1 '(9)Ἁλληλουιά' = Heb 113:9). All are recorded verbatim as '# margin: ...' / '# in-text: ... before WORD' comment lines in the page files, directly above the printed line, ready for a later conversion. NEEDED LATER FOR ENGLISH ANCHORS: psalm map LXX 1-8 = Heb 1-8; 9 = 9-10 (9:1-21 = Heb 9, 9:22-39 = Heb 10:1-18); 10-112 = Heb 11-113; 113 = Heb 114 (113:1-8) + 115 (113:9-26 = 115:1-18); 114 = Heb 116:1-9; 115 = Heb 116:10-19; 116-145 = Heb 117-146; 146 = Heb 147:1-11; 147 = Heb 147:12-20; 148-150 = 148-150; 151 has no Hebrew/English counterpart. Verse offsets: English Bibles leave titles unnumbered, Hebrew counts them; Swete (like the Hebrew) counts the title as verse 1 when it is long enough to have its own number, so in titled psalms Swete's verse n is usually English n-1 (and n-2 where the Hebrew title spans two verses, e.g. Ps 50, 51, 53, 59 where Swete prints 2 inside the title); where the title runs on into a margin 1 the numbers match English. A conversion would need per-psalm offsets (derivable from the # margin/in-text comments plus the {T}/{2} pattern) and owner decisions on how to show titles and the missing B verses.
